title: Chicken Kebabs
description:
A riff on tandoori-style chicken, these chicken kebabs are marinated with yogurt and lemon, with smoked and hot paprika in place of the more traditional Indian spice blend. The result is a completely different, but equally delicious, dish. Using chicken thighs instead of chicken breasts results in juicier and more flavorful kebabs. The yogurt in the marinade helps keep the chicken from drying out over high direct heat. A mixture of both smoked and hot paprika gives a delicious smoky and spicy flavor, plus an attractive red color.
You could also use some vegetable “spacers,” such as red onion, red or yellow peppers, anise slices, or cherry tomatoes. Tzatziki sauce is also good for dipping. Maybe serve with some cauliflower rice.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon finely grated peeled fresh ginger
2 teaspoons freshly minced garlic (about 2 medium cloves)
2 pounds skinless, boneless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
directions: Whisk together yogurt, lemon juice, oil, ginger, salt, smoked paprika, hot paprika, garlic, black pepper, cumin, and cayenne pepper in a medium bowl. Place chicken in a large resealable plastic bag. Pour in marinade (maybe reserving some) and seal bag, removing as much air as possible. Place in refrigerator and marinate for a while, preferably 4 to 8 hours.
Maybe use a little marinade for some vegetables on the skewer.
Thread chicken (and maybe vegetables) onto skewers.

Allow to grill to get hot. Clean and oil the grilling grate. Grill skewers until well browned on all sides and center of chicken registers between 160-165°F on an instant read thermometer, 3-4 minutes per side.
Transfer skewers to platter and let rest for 5 minutes. Serve immediately.
